root_cause_isolation.source: this session, live on-device, 5 minimal confirming/refuting probes
root_cause_isolation.conclusion: The failure is NOT about {m,n} syntax specifically, NOT about nesting depth, and NOT about inline-vs-named character classes. It IS specifically: a mandatory character-class term immediately followed by an OPTIONAL/repeated character-class-derived continuation (whichever way that optionality is spelled - native {0,N}, or a manually expanded nested-optional group). This exact shape ([1-9] [0-9]{0,N} and everything downstream of it) is what task 5's boundedIntRule primitive generates for every bounded integer field across all four schemas (duration, days_int, quota_int, target_int, importance, etc.) - so this is not a task_extraction-specific bug.

probes.hypothesis_tested: does naming the repeated character class first fix it?
probes.outcome: REFUTED - still fails even with the class named.

probes.hypothesis_tested: is the bare (...)? optional-group operator supported at all?
probes.outcome: CONFIRMED supported - single-level optional groups over string literals work fine.

probes.hypothesis_tested: does 3-level nesting itself break it, independent of character classes?
probes.outcome: REFUTED - same nesting depth as the failing duration case, pure literals, parses and generates fine.

probes.hypothesis_tested: is zero-minimum repetition on a character class the trigger?
probes.outcome: REFUTED - a lone [0-9]{0,4} (zero-min) parses fine when it's the only character class in the rule.

probes.hypothesis_tested: do two adjacent character classes fail even with zero repetition/optionality?
probes.outcome: REFUTED - fully mandatory adjacent classes (no optionality at all) parse and generate fine.
